articles.title: Is Kyrie Irving the perfect partner for Cooper Flagg?
articles.summary: Here's what a healthy Irving could unlock for Flagg and the Mavericks this season.
articles.body:
The Dallas Mavericks overhauled their front office, hired a new head coach, and reshaped their roster this offseason. But their most important addition on the court could be Kyrie Irving as he returns from a torn ACL. If Kyrie looks like Kyrie, no one will benefit more than Cooper Flagg, who has apparently grown .

Former head coach Jason Kidd spent the start of last season experimenting with Flagg playing point guard. A lot of the time, Flagg looked like a teenager. But by the end of the season, Flagg looked like an All-NBA player. Over his final 26 games, Flagg averaged 25.2 points, 7.2 rebounds, and 5.3 assists. His surge was highlighted by a 51-point performance that helped him win Rookie of the Year.

By bringing the ball up the floor, using screens and reading defenders over hundreds of repetitions, he's better prepared for his career moving forward. However, Flagg and the Mavericks were better when he played with a pure point guard.

When Flagg shared the floor with Ryan Nembhard or Brandon Williams last season, he was more efficient and the Mavericks played better. This doesn't mean that Flagg can't run an offense. It just means that, at least at this stage of his career, he's better when he has help. That's why Irving's mere presence can provide balance to Flagg's offensive diet.

Flagg's magic is that he can be both an initiator and a play finisher. He can grab a rebound and lead the break, run pick-and-roll or attack from the elbows. But he can also cut, screen, roll, spot up, crash the glass and destroy a rotating defense.

Kyrie has already shown he can thrive alongside jumbo playmakers. He won a championship next to LeBron James and excelled alongside Luka Dončić . And though Flagg is nowhere near as accomplished as LeBron or Luka, he brings a versatile skill set that can complement Kyrie. On some plays, Irving can run the show while Flagg moves around off-ball. On other plays, it'll be Flagg who handles the ball and Kyrie can set an inverted screen for him.

Obviously, there's concern around whether Kyrie can stay healthy. He's 34 years old and just missed a full calendar year. But Cooper is the centerpiece now. And together, they're going to have plenty of help.

At center, Daniel Gafford and Dereck Lively II ( who is still recovering from foot surgery ) provide two vertical threats. There's concern over Lively's durability, but that's why drafting Morez Johnson Jr. made so much sense. Johnson is an elite athlete who can switch across positions as a 6-foot-9, 250-pound defender. The Mavericks also brought in Santi Aldama , who is a floor-spacing forward that can do a lot of the little things. P.J. Washington , Max Christie , and Naji Marshall remain on the roster and offer size and versatility — and, who knows, maybe a change of scenery even helps Zaccharie Risacher find a stable rotation role.

Now it's on new head coach Dusty May to put those pieces together. He led FAU to the Final Four and won a national championship in just his second season at Michigan. May said that Flagg will play "all over the court," which should really come as no surprise given how this roster is constructed. The new Dallas front office, led by Masai Ujiri and Mike Schmitz, is already surrounding Flagg with versatile pieces that could translate to immediate wins.

If Irving can return healthy, then we could see Flagg turn into a star and the Mavericks turn into a playoff team a lot sooner than anyone might expect.

articles.title: Un imparable TJ Shorts da la primera victoria al Valencia Basket
articles.standfirst: El base anota 26 puntos en el sufrido triunfo ante el Besiktas, que falló un triple para ganar sobre la bocina
articles.summary: El base anota 26 puntos en el sufrido triunfo ante el Besiktas, que falló un triple para ganar sobre la bocina
articles.body: TJ Shorts deslumbró hace dos temporadas jugando al ritmo frenético del París Basketball. La pasada, sufrió bajo la estructura de Ergin Ataman en el Panathinaikos. En la que acaba de comenzar con el Valencia Basket ya ha demostrado que se ha liberado de los grilletes y volverá a ser una estrella de la Euroliga. En el estreno de la competición, el pequeño base hizo 26 puntos para liderar el triunfo taronja en la visita al Besiktas (94-96). Suya fue la canasta de la victoria, aunque aún restaba más de un minuto en el que se vieron errores por cada bando, incluidos dos tiros libres fallados por Omoruyi para empatar y otros dos por Taylor para sentenciar. Los turcos se encontraron 15 segundos para un último ataque. Nowell tuvo un triple para ganar sobre la bocina. Falló. Triunfo del Valencia Basket. Buen estreno de Xavi Albert como primer entrenador taronja. Shorts destacó sobre todos en un Valencia con las mismas señas de identidad que en la etapa de Pedro Martínez, incluido el trabajo coral. El base y otros cinco jugadores alcanzaron la decena de puntos. Entre ellos, Nikola Mirotic, que debutó de naranja metiendo 13 y siendo importante mediado el último cuarto, cuando el Besiktas ya había remontado y amenazaba con despegarse. Seis puntos seguidos del ala-pívot y una falta forzada en ataque fueron determinantes. Este Valencia que alineó a seis de sus nuevas caras, superó con madurez dos momentos críticos, uno en el primer cuarto y otro en el último. En el periodo inicial se vio ocho abajo (27-19) después de recibir un 12-3. Tras un tiempo muerto y con la pausa entre cuartos de por medio, respondió con parcial de 0-11. Shorts ya había hecho de las suyas y Brooks (10) era su cómplice. Después tomaron el testigo Taylor (12) y Rivero (10). Todos ellos llegaron con 10 puntos al intermedio. Y el Valencia, tres arriba (51-54). El tercer acto le perteneció casi por completo a Shorts, que amenazó ya con dos triples seguidos. Hizo 14 de los 27 puntos de su equipo, que firmó un sensacional 5/8 desde el arco. Uno de esos aciertos fue de un Mirotic que se desperezaba. Tanta puntería le dio al Valencia hasta 12 de ventaja (69-81). Al Besiktas le salvó la bocina y tras la pausa clavó cinco triples seguidos con un Morgan entonadísimo (15 puntos con 5/6). La diferencia, pese a los esfuerzos de Sako bajo el aro, se enjugó en un santiamén. Omoruyi adelantó a los locales (88-86) mientras la defensa cara a cara de Ugurlu neutralizaba a Shorts. El Besiktas se fue 91-86 tras otro triple, ahora de Wilbekin. El otro momento crítico. Y ahí apareció Mirotic. Taylor empató a 94 a falta de 2:03 y Shorts, en sus únicos puntos en el último cuarto, anotó en una entrada culminada en un escorzo imposible. Canastón. El de la victoria. El base encaja a la perfección en este Valencia. Ya es el líder. 94.- Besiktas (27+24+20+23): DeJulius (4), Nowell (17), Jeffries (-) Omoruyi (17), Zizic (4) -cinco inicial- Dotson (9), Morgan (15), Ugurlu (3), Birsen (-), Wilbekin (12), Brown (7), Gabriel (6). 96.- Valencia Basket (28+26+27+15): Shorts (26), Saint-Supèry (7), Taylor (12), Osetkowski (1), Reuvers (5) -cinco inicial- Rivero (10), Sako (10), Brooks (10), Moore (2), Puerto (-), Cárdenas (-), Mirotic (13). Árbitros: Mehdi Difallah, Ioannis Foufis y Luka Kardum. Sin eliminados. Incidencias: partido correspondiente a la primera jornada de la fase regular de la Euroliga disputado en el pabellón Turkcell Basketball Development Center de Estambul.

articles.title: Damian Lillard Hyped by Blazers in Return from Achilles Injury, 'He Looks Phenomenal'
articles.summary: Portland Trail Blazers guard Damian Lillard is heading back to the court soon enough after missing all of last season with a torn left Achilles tendon suffered during the 2025 playoffs.
articles.body:
Portland Trail Blazers guard Damian Lillard is heading back to the court soon enough after missing all of last season with a torn left Achilles tendon suffered during the 2025 playoffs.

He's already gotten some work in this summer with NBA players in advance of his long-awaited return.

Needless to say, folks are in awe of his efforts, per remarks relayed by Jason Quick of The Athletic.

"He looks phenomenal," Blazers head coach Micah Nori told Quick. "Every time I see him shoot the ball, I think it's going in."

Nori added: "If I never knew Dame Lillard, and I came into the building and just started watching them play basketball, I would not be able to tell he had any type of surgery.

Blazers forward Toumani Camara also had this to say.

"Impressive. Very, very impressive." He also remarked: "I think the most impressive thing for me was his first step, his speed, especially coming back from that injury. He was just very hard to guard all around."

Quick reported that Lillard has been taking part in daily runs at the Blazers' facility. In addition, Nori told Quick that he believes Lillard will fully participate (i.e. no limitations or restrictions) when training camp starts Tuesday, Sept. 29. That remark occurred after Lillard (and the rest of the team) underwent physicals last Wednesday.

The 36-year-old Lillard is a nine-time All-Star and seven-time All-NBA player who has averaged 25.1 points and 6.7 assists over his 13 NBA seasons. The 75th Anniversary Team member played in Portland for 11 campaigns before a trade request sent him to the Milwaukee Bucks for two years.

Now Lillard is back with Portland on a three-year deal as he hopes to lead the Blazers to greater heights. Portland bottomed out at 21-61 in 2023-24 but rose to 36-46 in 2024-25 before making the playoffs as a 42-win No. 7 seed last year.

The arrow continues to point up with Lillard in the mix and the addition of Nori, a well-respected and long-time assistant coach finally getting his chance as a head coach. If Lillard returns anywhere close to (or at) his old form, then that's a massive win for a Portland team that brings back a young core which got this team to the playoffs last year. The addition of Ja Morant via trade should also help matters.

Portland begins the season on Wed., Oct. 21 vs. the Phoenix Suns. By all accounts, Lillard should be starting and welcomed back with open arms by the home crowd.

articles.title: La Supercopa femenina alza el telón con el nuevo clásico: Valencia-Zaragoza
articles.standfirst: Helena Pueyo, exjugadora del equipo maño, pone el morbo en la primera semifinal (17.15 horas) e Innova-tsn Leganés y Hozono Global Jairis se miden en la segunda (20.00 h.)
articles.summary: Helena Pueyo, exjugadora del equipo maño, pone el morbo en la primera semifinal (17.15 horas) e Innova-tsn Leganés y Hozono Global Jairis se miden en la segunda (20.00 h.)
articles.body: La temporada nacional en el baloncesto femenino echa a andar este sábado con las semifinales de la Supercopa, que se disputará en el pabellón Jorge Garbajosa de Torrejón de Ardoz. Valencia Basket, Casademont Zaragoza, Hozono Global Jairis e Innova.tsn Leganés, que ejercerá de anfitrión, lucharán por el primer título del curso. En semifinales, duelo estelar entre dos de las grandes potencias del baloncesto femenino español en las últimas temporadas: Valencia Basket vs Casademont Zaragoza (17.15 horas). Ambos se han visto las caras recientemente luchando por títulos. De hecho, se midieron en las dos últimas finales de la Supercopa. Las taronjas ganaron en 2024 y las mañas, el año pasado. También será la reedición de las dos últimas finales de la Liga Femenina Endesa. Ahí vencieron las valencianas, que suman cuatro entorchados consecutivos. Con Javier Torralba iniciando nueva era en el banquillo esperan mantener ese dominio. En el epicentro del duelo estará la internacional Helena Pueyo, MVP de la última Supercopa, que este verano cambió Zaragoza por Valencia. El destino ha querido que su debut oficial como jugadora taronja sea contra sus ex. "Es algo emotivo por mis dos últimas temporadas", admitió la jugadora mallorquina en su presentación con su nuevo equipo. Enfrente, entre otras rivales, estará Mariona Ortiz, con la que ha compartido vestuario en la selección durante el Mundial de Berlín, cerrado con un bronce. Aprovechar el tirón de ese éxito es otro de los objetivos de la temporada. La segunda semifinal medirá a las anfitrionas del Innova.tsn Leganés y al Hozono Global Jairis (20.00 horas). Dos equipos buscarán dar la campanada en un torneo abierto y en el que los grandes no han alcanzado aún todo su potencial. La gran final, este domingo a las 17.00 horas. Todos los partidos se podrán ver por Teledeporte.

articles.title: Damian Lillard Drops New Song 'Nothing Without You' With Souls of Mischief, More
articles.summary: Damian Lillard is dropping more music ahead of his return to the Portland Trail Blazers.
articles.body:
Damian Lillard is dropping more music ahead of his return to the Portland Trail Blazers.

Lillard, under his stage name Dame D.O.L.L.A., collaborated with 1999 WRITE THE FUTURE and Souls of Mischief on a new song titled "Nothing Without You."

The latest single comes about five weeks after Lillard released a five-song collection titled Houston, We Have A Problem .

These latest projects come almost a decade after Lillard dropped his first full-length album, The Letter O, in 2016.

Lillard sat out the entirety of the 2025-26 season after suffering a torn left Achilles tendon in his final game with the Milwaukee Bucks.

He is preparing to open training camp next week before potentially seeing his first NBA action in over a year Oct. 21 during the Blazers' home opener against the Phoenix Suns.

articles.title: A’ja Wilson ‘flattens’ arena staffer before Aces game, shocking collision sparks stunned reactions from teammates and fans
articles.summary: WNBA star A’ja Wilson was involved in an awkward accident before the Las Vegas Aces faced the Phoenix Mercury on Thursday night, when she collided with an
articles.body: WNBA star A’ja Wilson was involved in an awkward accident before the Las Vegas Aces faced the Phoenix Mercury on Thursday night, when she collided with an arena staff member in the tunnel. Video from the scene showed the woman walking near a curtain as the Aces came out toward the court. Wilson ran into her, sending the staffer to the floor, while teammates reacted to the sudden collision. The woman quickly got back up, and the Aces continued to the court. Wilson then scored 34 points as Las Vegas completed a 100-82 regular-season win.A’ja Wilson collides with arena staffer as Las Vegas Aces enter courtThe incident happened before tipoff at the Mortgage Matchup Center in Phoenix. The video showed an arena staffer walking in front of a large curtain just as the Las Vegas players were preparing to run onto the court.Wilson was at the front of the group when she came through the curtain and collided with the woman. The impact sent the staffer to the floor. Chelsea Gray was visible behind Wilson and appeared to react to what had happened.According to the Daily Mail, the woman was able to stand up almost immediately. There was no report in the material reviewed of a serious injury to the staff member.The short clip then spread across X, where viewers focused on how the collision happened. One user wrote: ‘No, why is that lady there?! No one warned her the team are running out.’Another fan asked: ‘Why was she walking past in that moment anyways???’A third wrote: ‘Bruh… why was she just casually walking in front of it.’One viewer took the concern in another direction, writing: ‘Imagine injuring the greatest player of all time just before the playoffs sheesh.’A’ja Wilson scores 34 as Las Vegas Aces beat Phoenix MercuryWilson did not appear affected by the incident once the game began. She scored 17 points in the first quarter and had 21 by halftime as Las Vegas built a 65-36 lead.She made 16 of 28 shots, and her scoring helped Las Vegas build an early cushion.The Aces went on to beat the Phoenix Mercury 100-82 and finished the regular season with a 31-13 record. Wilson led the way with 34 points, while Jewell Loyd added 25 points off the bench. Stephanie Talbot scored 14 and Chelsea Gray had 12 points.The Associated Press reported that Las Vegas shot 56 per cent from the field and had 28 assists. The result left the Aces as the No. 3 seed for the WNBA playoffs, with Indiana Fever waiting in the first round.Phoenix ended its season at 16-28 after the loss. articles.title: Warriors' Podziemski Could Crack ESPN's NBA Top 100 Next Season
articles.summary: According to ESPN's Zach Kram, Brandin Podziemski could crack ESPN's top-100 players next season, if he can make some improvements to his game.
articles.body:
Since entering the NBA as the 19th pick in the 2023 NBA Draft, Brandin Podziemski has carved out a solid role for himself within the Golden State Warriors rotation. He's proven himself to be a versatile talent capable of playing multiple positions and a range of roles. Yet, despite his versatility, Podziemski is often underrated by fans and the media alike.

Despite being overlooked for his contributions, ESPN's Zach Kram believes that if Podziemski can continue improving his game, he could break into ESPN's top-100 players by next summer.

"Even if Podziemski is unlikely ever to develop into a star, his all-around solid play makes him a valuable contributor," Kram wrote. "He can make open 3s, support Stephen Curry with secondary playmaking and hold his own on the defensive end. Even a moderate improvement in his age-23 season should place him firmly in Top 100 consideration next year."

Last season, Podziemski averaged 13.8 points, 5.1 rebounds and 3.7 assists, shooting 53.1 percent from 2-point range and 37.1 percent from deep. Impressively, he played in all 82 regular-season games for Golden State, while posting a career-high 28.5 minutes per night.

Podziemski has become a key contributor for Kerr, emerging as a connector and high-level role player. It shouldn't take too much of a developmental leap for him to crack the NBA . Whether that changes how Podziemski is viewed by fans outside of the Warriors bubble is another question entirely, and in truth, shouldn't matter too much, especially if he helps Golden State make some noise in the postseason.

This post originally appeared on Warriors Wire ! Follow us on Facebook and Twitter !

articles.title: LeBron James Snub Discussed by Cavs' Koby Altman, Exec Says 'Teams Got Better to Chase Us'
articles.summary: The Cleveland Cavaliers were on LeBron James' shortlist in free agency this year, but in the end, the four-time MVP decided chose against a third stint with his old team and joined the Philadelphia 76ers.
articles.body:
The Cleveland Cavaliers were on LeBron James' shortlist in free agency this year, but in the end, the four-time MVP decided chose against a third stint with his old team and joined the Philadelphia 76ers.

However, the Cavs are confident despite James heading elsewhere, per comments by team president Koby Altman, who spoke with reporters at a press conference Friday (h/t Joe Reedy of the Associated Press).

"I'd be more worried if I was worried about talent, our process or some of the more day-to-day things," Altman said. "I think a lot of teams got better to chase us. When you're a final four team, teams need to improve to get to that level. And we're on that level. We want more."

NBA Exec: Luka Can Reach 'Full Potential'

The 52-win Cavaliers did finish as a top-four team, making the Eastern Conference Finals after a pair of seven-game playoff series wins against the No. 5 seed Toronto Raptors and No. 1 seed Detroit Pistons. However, the eventual NBA champion New York Knicks swept the Cavs in four games in the East Finals.

Credit to the Cavs, of course, for getting as far as they've gone in the playoffs without James on the roster since 1992. They have a strong core of talent in place led by Donovan Mitchell, who signed a four-year extension. James Harden signed a three-year extension, and Peyton Watson is now aboard via trade from the Denver Nuggets. Big men Evan Mobley and Jarrett Allen are back in town.

"You go through the list and zoom out and say, 'OK, was this offseason a success? Were we able to get better? Did we look at the future? Did we get more financial flexibility, more sustainability with the roster?' All of those things lead me to say this was a really good offseason in spite of that one decision," Altman said.

One can argue, though, that the Cavs were still far away from the championship picture given how poorly the Eastern Conference Finals went. Although head coach Kenny Atkinson said the Cavs were "analytically" winning the series 2-1 after Game 3, ultimately, Cleveland fell 4-0 and got outscored by 77 points.

Still, the Cavs are one of the better Eastern Conference teams on paper, and Altman is confident in his team despite James picking Philly.

"We can't be reliant on one outcome. I think we have too much of a good thing going in terms of our infrastructure, our foundation to worry about one outcome," Altman said at a news conference Friday before the Cavaliers begin training camp next week. "I'm not downplaying the enormity and magnitude of the decision. I just think the way we're built as an organization is we have a great foundation and a great sort of ecosystem in terms of talent, coaching staff, our performance staff and we're built for a sustainable run here regardless of one outcome."

Cleveland will visit James and the 76ers to begin the season in Philadelphia on Oct. 22.

articles.title: Steph Curry, Warriors Agree to New Contract, Latest Rumors on Deal as Superstar Takes Less Than Max
articles.summary: Twelve-time NBA All-Star Stephen Curry reaffirmed his commitment to the Golden State Warriors.
articles.body:
Twelve-time NBA All-Star Stephen Curry reaffirmed his commitment to the Golden State Warriors.

The two sides have agreed to a two-year, $116 million extension with a player option for 2028-29, per Shams Charania of ESPN.

Curry was originally set to be a free agent next summer and was eligible for up to $136.7 million over two years on his next deal.

General manager Mike Dunleavy Jr. praised Curry after signing the new deal:

While the idea of the four-time champion playing for another team is jarring, there's no getting around the state of the Warriors right now.

Golden State went 37-45 in 2025-26 and couldn't navigate out of the play-in tournament.

Sure, the Warriors likely would've had a better record if Curry appeared in more than 43 games, but all roads mostly led to the same point. Golden State is no longer a strong championship contender as currently constructed.

The organization is staking a lot on 36-year-old Jimmy Butler bouncing back from a torn ACL. It also needs Curry to stay healthy and remain near his peak.

And even having Butler and Curry deliver may not be enough.

There's a reason Dunleavy went after Giannis Antetokounmpo prior to the 2026 trade deadline. According to ESPN's Ramona Shelburne , the Warriors were willing to send four first-round picks to the Milwaukee Bucks.

For as much as Antetokounmpo would help, acquiring a player of that caliber would require sacrificing Butler or franchise icon Draymond Green. There's no other way to realistically add a big salary to the books .

The idea of bringing both Anthony Davis and LeBron James to the Bay Area quickly died on the vine. The fact it even got to the discussion phase spoke volumes.

Bob Myers saw the challenges that lay ahead stepped down as GM in May 2023. Nobody can blame him for ducking out and leaving Dunleavy as the one holding the bag.

Resolution on one front at least came when coach Steve Kerr signed a new two-year contract. His future on the sideline was a storyline all last year, and some assumed his decision would impact the thinking of his best player.

Curry and Kerr have a rapport that transcends the typical coach/player dynamic. Their legacies are intertwined.

Last fall, Curry told ESPN's Anthony Slater he didn't want to play for another coach.

"We deserve that, I feel," he said. "Things change in this league. We can only control so much. But I think we're in a very unique situation that we deserve the opportunity [to ride it out]."

Once Kerr signed his new deal, that put to bed the immediate concerns about Curry's status. Kerr walking away would've had a lot of fans on edge.

If winning another title is his overriding goal, then Curry's best shot is in a different setting. The Warriors simply aren't there at the moment and don't have an easy path to get there.

By agreeing to a new contract, Curry is putting a lot of faith in the front office, or perhaps his desire to spend his entire career with one team is outweighing the satisfaction of chasing a fifth championship.

Either way, the news is cause for celebration in the short term. The fanbase is justified in getting excited, even if some of the big-picture questions remain unanswered.

articles.title: “It REALLY means EVERYTHING to me”: Bronny James gets heartwarming message from teary-eyed LeBron James as the father son duo enters NBA rivalry in 2026-27 season
articles.summary: Bronny James shared another memorable summer with his father, LeBron James, but one recent moment carried a little more weight as the father-son duo
articles.body: Bronny James shared another memorable summer with his father, LeBron James, but one recent moment carried a little more weight as the father-son duo prepares to enter a new NBA chapter. LeBron posted a collection of photos and videos from their time together on the golf course, offering a glimpse of a quieter side of their relationship away from basketball. The post quickly stood out for more than the family pictures. In his caption, the NBA star opened up about how deeply these moments with his son mean to him, revealing just how emotional their time together can become.LeBron's message came as the James family enjoyed one of the final stretches of a summer before their basketball paths separate. Golf has given father and son another way to spend time together, with Bronny's swing even drawing attention from NBA fans and a professional golfer. Soon, though, the two will no longer share the same NBA team. LeBron is preparing for his first season with the Philadelphia 76ers, while Bronny enters his third NBA season without his father beside him on the court.Bronny James shares a special summer with LeBron before a major NBA changeLeBron's Instagram reel, posted Thursday night, brought together several moments from the summer, with the father and son playing golf while Roy Ayers Ubiquity's “Everybody Loves The Sunshine” played in the background.The images captured a relaxed side of their relationship. For LeBron, though, the significance went much deeper than a few rounds of golf.“Can’t tell you how special times like these are for me being a dad! S–t damn near had me in tears out there yesterday afternoon,” LeBron wrote. “Never had these moments growing up so it REALLY means EVERYTHING to me. LOVE BEING A DAD!”The message offered a personal glimpse into why these ordinary moments have become so meaningful for the 41-year-old NBA star. LeBron has spent much of his life in the spotlight, but the post focused on something far more personal: simply having time with his son.The photos and videos were captured by Abigail Keenan Field, a former Lakers photographer who now works as a freelancer. LeBron tagged her in the post and thanked her for documenting the day, writing, “Thank you for capturing the moment.”Basketball has always been central to the James family's life, but golf has become another shared activity for LeBron and Bronny. The two were also seen playing together in May after the Lakers were eliminated from the playoffs by the Oklahoma City Thunder.Bronny's game on the golf course even attracted attention. Fans compared his swing to Rory McIlroy's, while professional golfer Michael S. Kim offered his own assessment, calling it “a really solid swing.”LeBron James and Bronny James begin separate NBA chaptersThe summer moments also arrived at an important point for both father and son.LeBron will not return to the Lakers for the upcoming season after signing with the Philadelphia 76ers. The move marks his first season away from Los Angeles in eight years and creates a new dynamic for the James family.For Bronny, the change is equally notable. The 22-year-old guard is entering his third NBA season, but for the first time since his USC days, he will not be sharing a basketball court with his father.The father-son pairing has been one of the most closely followed stories around the James family since Bronny entered the NBA. articles.title: Stephen Curry Will Make NBA History in Career Earnings After New Warriors Contract
articles.summary: Stephen Curry is on track to become the highest-paid player in NBA history in terms of career earnings after signing a historic extension with the Golden State Warriors.
articles.body:
Stephen Curry is on track to become the highest-paid player in NBA history in terms of career earnings after signing a historic extension with the Golden State Warriors.

The Warriors announced Friday Curry had signed an extension, which ESPN's Shams Charania reported is a two-year, $116 million deal with a player option for 2028-29.

Ranking the NBA's Best Young Cores Right Now 🔢

Curry was heading into the 2026-27 season on a one-year, $62.3 million contract that brought his career earnings to around $532 million, per Spotrac .

Spotrac then projects Curry will be playing under a $55.8 million cap hit in 2027-28 and hold a $58 million cap hit for the following campaign.

The extension will put Curry on track to earn around $645 million by the end of the 2028-29 season. By that time he is projected to become the highest-paid NBA player of all time by Spotrac .

No other player is currently on track to make more than $600 million in career earnings, according to Spotrac.

The extension will for now put Curry on track to beat out Kevin Durant and LeBron James, who Spotrac projects are on track to receive $591 million and $589 million in career salary, respectively.

Curry, Durant and James are the only players on track to finish out the upcoming season with more than $500 million in career earnings. Spotrac projects that by 2031 this trio will be joined in the half-billion club by players including Kawhi Leonard, Devin Booker, Paul George, Donovan Mitchell, Joel Embiid and James Harden.

The Warriors will hope Curry will be able to start out his final season before his new extension by bouncing by from the right knee issues that impacted his 2025-26 campaign when his team opens the regular season Oct. 21 at the Los Angeles Lakers.

articles.title: Stephen Curry signs 2-year, $116 million extension to stay in Golden State
articles.summary: Stephen Curry was only eligible to add 2 years to his existing contract due to the NBA's "over-38 rule."
articles.body:
Stephen Curry has agreed to a two-year, $116 million contract extension with the Golden State Warriors , according to ESPN's Shams Charania — a re-up in line to keep the two-time NBA Most Valuable Player and future Hall of Famer with the team that drafted him through his 20th professional season.

The team confirmed the extension on Friday, but did not provide details. The deal reportedly includes a player option in the 2028-29 season, per Charania.

Curry could add a maximum of two years to his existing contract due to the "over-38 rule" in the collective bargaining agreement between the NBA's teams and players union. Tacking two more years at 35% of the projected salary cap line — the maximum wage he's eligible to command as a player with 10 or more years of NBA service time — onto the one-year, $62.6 million extension he signed back in 2024 will bring the total value of Steph's current contract to $178.6 million through the end of the 2028-29 campaign. (Add that to the new 10-year, $400 million endorsement deal with Li-Ning , and it's been an awfully lucrative summer for your man Steph.)

That would be Curry's 20th season as a Warrior. Only 12 players in NBA history have played 20 or more seasons. Only three — Dirk Nowitzki , Kobe Bryant and Udonis Haslem — have spent the entire span with one franchise.

Across nearly two decades in the Bay Area, Curry has effectively resurrected the Warriors, restoring the once-proud organization of Wilt Chamberlain and Rick Barry to the consistent contention that preceded the largely fallow '80s, '90s and Aughts. Yes, he's had plenty of help along the way: from Mark Jackson and Steve Kerr, from Splash Brother Klay Thompson and defensive complement Draymond Green , from Swiss Army knife Andre Iguodala and championship guarantor Kevin Durant , plus many more.

More than any of them, though, it's Curry who redefined how the franchise could feel and the heights to which it could aspire. In the process, he helped change the very shape of the sport in the modern era, revolutionizing the geometry of offense — and necessitating a counter-revolution in defensive strategy and tactics. That is all thanks to the unprecedented accuracy, volume, speed and depth of his 3-point shooting, whether pulling up off the dribble or slaloming through off-ball screens before relocating for a catch-and-shoot look.

The gifts that made Curry a collegiate sensation at Davidson and the No. 7 pick in the 2009 NBA Draft — right after the Timberwolves selected a pair of point guards, Ricky Rubio and Jonny Flynn, much to Minnesotans' chagrin, and right before the Knicks ' No. 8 slot, much to New Yorkers' — immediately translated, as he averaged 18 points on 47/44/91 shooting splits and 5.9 assists per game across his first two seasons.

But after persistent right ankle injuries cost him 40 games in his third year and resulted in season-ending surgery, concerns over whether the young sharpshooter might be too big an injury risk to bank on limited him to just a four-year, $44 million extension of his rookie-scale contract.

"My ankle was a big factor in the [contract extension] number," Curry told Yahoo Sports' Marc J. Spears at the time . "They had to protect themselves a little bit."

That hedge-your-bets figure would wind up being one of the most consequential bargains in NBA history.

After getting scar tissue removed from the troublesome ankle and setting about a stem-to-stern revamping of his core, hip and ankle strength , Curry transformed into one of the league's most durable and productive superstars. He has averaged 20 or more points per game in each of the last 14 seasons; only six players in NBA history ( LeBron James , Durant, Karl Malone, Kareem Abdul-Jabbar, Bryant and Michael Jordan) have more 20-plus-point campaigns over the course of their careers.

Curry is one of 44 players in NBA history to win at least four championships , one of 29 players ever to make at least 12 All-Star teams, one of 22 with at least 11 All-NBA/ABA selections , one of 19 with multiple scoring titles , one of 16 with multiple MVP trophies , and one of just six with four rings, multiple MVPs and a Finals MVP . He was also the first, and to date only, unanimous MVP in league history. There are 10 seasons of 300 or more made 3-pointers in NBA history; Curry owns six of them , including the only 400 -triple campaign on record.

While the former "baby-faced assassin" has continued to produce at an All-Star/All-NBA level through his mid-to-late 30s, the Warriors have slipped from their dynastic perch since their 2022 title , winning two playoff series in the past four years. Last season, waylaid by injuries to both Curry and fellow superstar Jimmy Butler , Golden State finished under .500 for just the second time since the 2011 lockout.

After a home-run-swing bid to add LeBron James fell short at the warning track, the Warriors seem to be stuck — long on aging veterans, light on notable young talent, projected to remain mired in the play-in picture in the Western Conference.

That somewhat grim near-future outlook led some to wonder whether Curry might consider seeking greener pastures in a bid for a fifth championship as he walks the back-nine of his legendary career. But Golden State brass projected confidence that he'd want to stay the course, and Curry — a "realist" who understands the franchise's predicament — reportedly maintained a desire to remain with the only franchise he's ever known.

This agreement removes any doubt about those desires. Wherever the Warriors go next, and whoever and whatever they want to be, they'll continue to revolve around Curry for the foreseeable future. Same as it ever was.

articles.title: Stephen Curry’s wife Ayesha Curry opens up on finding joy in "life’s little pleasures" as she reflects on her $50 million brand
articles.summary: Stephen Curry, the Golden State Warriors’ star player, has had his wife, Ayesha Curry, by his side for over the last two decades.
articles.body: Stephen Curry, the Golden State Warriors’ star player, has had his wife, Ayesha Curry, by his side for over the last two decades. While Stephen Curry was building his career in the league, Ayesha Curry stood by his side and their children. But she always wanted to carve out her own career path. Ahead of the new season, Stephen Curry’s wife Ayesha Curry reflected on her skincare brand, Sweet July.Stephen Curry’s wife Ayesha Curry reflects on what inspired her to name her successful skincare brand Sweet July A few months ago, in an interview with Vogue, Stephen Curry’s wife Ayesha Curry opened up about the reason why her brand name is Sweet July.She reflected on the month of July as she said, “I just noticed that it would be such a heightened time of joy, and I was like, I wanna feel this amount of joy every single day and why can’t I? The small things in life should bring me joy…”The popular actress and chef added, “It doesn’t have to be a birthday or an anniversary. My morning cup of coffee should bring me this joy, or my skincare routine should bring me this joy, so we created this mantra to like find joy in life’s little pleasures.”For the unversed, Stephen Curry and Ayesha Curry tied the knot in the month of July in 2009 after dating for several years.Later, the high profile couple welcomed three of their children in the month of July spanning different years.Stephen Curry’s wife Ayesha Curry’s popular skincare brand is inspired from her Jamaican heritage and what she has learned from her familyLaunched in 2023, Ayesha Curry’s skincare brand Sweet July has been highly successful among the masses as a lot of it has been inspired from what she has learned about her Jamaican roots.In the same interview with Vogue, Stephen Curry’s wife Ayesha Curry reflected on what she has learned from her ancestors as she said, “Growing up, I just remember them always having these little old wives tails about their skincare like, ‘Rub this tomato on your face, like it'll be good for you,’ or ‘Take this aloe vera and put it on after the sun…’”It has been over three years since Ayesha Curry launched her brand and it has only grown successfully since then.Stephen Curry and Ayesha Curry have also launched cafes in Charlotte inspired by the Jamaican theme as they expand their investment portfolio.With just a few days left for the new season to begin, the four time NBA champion Stephen Curry remains focused on his recovery and a desire to make a successful comeback to the field after his injury plagued season.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Why Stephen Curry extension was right move for Warriors
articles.summary: There are moments when an NBA franchise has to choose between cold basketball economics and its own identity. Golden State faced exactly that crossroads with...
articles.body:
There are moments when an NBA franchise has to choose between cold basketball economics and its own identity. Golden State faced exactly that crossroads with superstar Stephen Curry . The Warriors ultimately chose to extend the relationship that transformed the franchise while finding a way to preserve financial flexibility. Curry agreed to a two-year, $116 million extension with a player option for 2028-29. This essentially keeps him in Golden State through at least the 2027-28 season. The contract comes with obvious age-related risk, particularly as Curry approaches his 40s. However, the structure matters as much as the headline number. Curry accepted less than his projected two-year maximum. This gave Golden State additional room under the NBA's increasingly punitive second-apron restrictions. This was a calculated attempt to keep an elite offensive force and preserve enough maneuverability to keep competing.

The Warriors entered the 2026 offseason knowing their margin for error was shrinking. Golden State explored the possibility of adding LeBron James but ultimately missed out. James signed with Philadelphia instead. Draymond Green subsequently returned on a one-year, $27.7 million contract. The organization also retained much of its veteran infrastructure. Kristaps Porziņģis agreed to a two-year, $40 million deal. Al Horford , De'Anthony Melton, and Gary Payton II also returned. Golden State then added Yaxel Lendeborg with the 11th overall selection. This gave the veteran-heavy roster a younger, versatile frontcourt option.

That strategy made Curry's extension even more important. The Warriors were never positioned for a clean reset. The organization instead chose to maximize whatever remains of its competitive window while gradually introducing younger pieces around him. The extension fits that philosophy perfectly.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

There is no ordinary comparison for Curry. Everyone knows that. Selected seventh overall by Golden State in 2009, he became the central figure in one of the NBA's defining dynasties. He has won four championships, two regular-season MVP awards, and the 2022 Finals MVP. He has also firmly established himself as the NBA's all-time leader in made three-pointers .

Of course, Curry fundamentally changed how basketball is played. The extreme range, constant movement, and gravitational pull forced defenses to rethink traditional concepts of spacing. That remains valuable even as Curry ages. His greatest weapons, which are shooting, balance, footwork, anticipation and off-ball movement, are skills that can remain effective even when the physical margins inevitably narrow.

The most important part of Curry's extension is what Golden State avoided paying. Curry was eligible for a projected two-year maximum extension worth roughly $136.7 million. The agreement instead gives him $116 million. That represents a significant discount from that maximum.

Under the modern CBA, it matters considerably. The Warriors have been operating in an increasingly restrictive financial environment. Every dollar below the second-apron thresholds can affect their ability to retain players, make trades, and maintain roster flexibility. Curry accepting less than his maximum therefore gives Golden State additional room to maneuver around the most expensive portion of its roster. It gives Mike Dunleavy Jr . a little more oxygen. That could become critical at the trade deadline or during future roster decisions.

The obvious counterargument is Curry's age. He will enter the 2026-27 season at 38. Curry missed 27 games with a knee injury last season. Golden State finished 37-45 and failed to advance from the Play-In Tournament. Those concerns are legitimate, but they do not erase the value of having Curry available.

Even when his athleticism inevitably declines, the attention he commands remains extraordinary. His presence creates opportunities for teammates before he even touches the ball. That effect can elevate players such as Butler, Green, Porziņģis, and Brandin Podziemski simply because opposing defenses cannot afford to lose track of Curry. And unlike a traditional aging scorer, Curry does not need to dominate the ball to influence a possession.

There is also a franchise-level consideration that cannot be separated from the basketball decision. Curry is synonymous with the modern Warriors. His No. 30 jersey, global popularity, and connection with the Bay Area have become part of Golden State's broader identity. Extending him through the next stage of his career ensures the franchise's most recognizable player remains in the uniform that became inseparable from his legacy. The Warriors are preserving continuity around the player most responsible for making Golden State a global basketball brand.

The Curry extension carries risk, sure. However, the structure makes the wager considerably more sensible. Curry stayed with the franchise that drafted him. Golden State retained its defining star. And, crucially, the Warriors did not have to pay the full projected maximum to make it happen. The deal protects both sides. Curry receives significant security for the final phase of his career. Golden State preserves additional financial flexibility to construct a competitive roster around him.

That is the real reason the extension works. Curry's final chapter may not replicate the dynasty's greatest years because it does not need to. For Golden State, keeping its greatest modern player in uniform while securing the financial flexibility to keep building around him was the most logical path forward. It is a calculated commitment to one more chapter of the Warriors' most important story.
